addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- lcars: The one LCARS entry point — "do the right thing" from the current state. With nothing filed it takes a free-form idea and files a Mission (the Align flow); with work in flight and nothing pending it drives the active Mission forward (auto-advance); with a decision waiting it opens the inbox. A shared resolver picks the target Mission so the captain never juggles ids — one candidate needs none, several drop into a picker, an explicit id / partial / title always works. Use when the user runs `lcars` (no verb), says "what should I do next", "continue", "pick up where I left off", or otherwise hands LCARS work without naming a stage.
- lcars-answer: The LCARS inbox — every pending decision across ALL Missions in one list, and one place to clear each. Surfaces scope escalations, plan-review stand-offs, blocked tickets, and the Verify ship/send-back gate; each card shows the Mission, the question, and its actions. It absorbs `lcars respond` (answer an escalation), `lcars approve` (ship a Verify card), and `lcars feedback` (send one back) as card actions, delegating to the scripts already built. Use when the user runs `lcars answer`, asks what needs an answer / what's waiting on them, or wants to approve, send back, or respond to a Mission without juggling ids.
- lcars-approve: Ship a verified LCARS Mission — MERGE its open pull request and mark it Done. Runs only on a Mission parked at the Verify stage, where `lcars run` has already AUTO-OPENED the PR and left the Mission "in review — PR open" (prUrl recorded in state.json). `lcars approve` is the captain's MERGE signal: it merges that open PR with `gh pr merge` (via the host adapter) and, only on a SUCCESSFUL merge, clears the stage labels, applies `lcars:done`, moves the stage to `done`, and prints the merged PR URL. It NEVER marks a Mission Done without a real merge — a failed merge (conflicts, checks, auth) leaves it at Verify with an actionable message (no false Done). With no open PR recorded it refuses (re-run the mission so Verify opens the PR first). Use when the captain runs `lcars approve <mission-id>`, or asks to approve / ship / merge the PR for a Mission they have finished reviewing in Verify.
- lcars-buddy: Your LCARS ride-along buddy — a companion you keep with you in ANY repo while you use LCARS, useful from day one and at every point after. Run it anytime (it's read-only and safe) to get extra detail the normal surfaces don't show: where the LCARS source sits and its git state, whether the installed skills actually match that checkout, and a live snapshot of the current repo's Mission(s) — stage, status, and recent events. It rides shotgun while everything's going fine (situational awareness, "what's actually happening under the hood"), and escalates naturally into a live-debug partner the moment something's off — diagnosing and fixing the LCARS source under LCARS's own build contract (author in skills/, TDD, ./install.sh, fast scoped tests). Use when the captain runs `lcars buddy`, wants a closer look / more detail on what LCARS is doing, is keeping a buddy around while driving a Mission elsewhere, or hits something that needs debugging or fixing in LCARS from another repo.
- lcars-feedback: Send an LCARS Mission back to Align with the captain's feedback — the Verify feedback loop. Appends the note to the Mission's feedback.md (a durable, accumulating history), resets the stage to `align`, and moves the GitHub label to `lcars:align`, while deleting none of the prior artifacts (PRD, research, validated/approved plans) so the next `lcars run` re-enters Align with the full history. Use when the captain runs `lcars feedback <mission-id> "<feedback>"`, or asks to send a Mission back / reject it with changes / re-align it after reviewing it in Verify.
- lcars-file: File a new LCARS Mission. Captures a free-form idea from the captain, runs an Align session to produce a PRD, then persists the mission under .git/lcars/missions/ and opens a labelled GitHub issue at the align stage. Use when the user runs `lcars file`, asks to start / file / open a new LCARS mission, feature, or bug.
- lcars-init: Initialize a repo for LCARS mission-based development. Scaffolds .git/lcars/ (config + missions dir), detects CONTEXT.md, verifies the Claude CLI, and creates the LCARS GitHub label set. Use when the user runs `lcars init`, asks to set up / bootstrap LCARS in a repo, or wants to prepare a repo for LCARS missions.
- lcars-launch: Get an LCARS Mission's app running locally so the captain can view it during Verify. `lcars launch <mission> [hint]` checks the mission's branch out into a disposable DETACHED git worktree, spawns a `launch`-role cold worker that DISCOVERS how to start the app (it never starts it itself), then the skill launches that command detached — owning the whole process group — writes a launch.json record both the CLI and the viewscreen daemon read, and prints an LCARS-voice readout naming the target, URL, and how to stop it. `lcars launch <mission> --stop` kills the process group and prunes the worktree. Failures are plain English, never a raw stack trace. Use when the captain runs `lcars launch`, asks to run / open / preview / see a mission's app while reviewing it, or wants to stop a launched app.
- lcars-log: Log bugs against an active LCARS Mission — the Mission Log. Takes free-form natural language describing one or more bugs found against a pre-merge Mission, extracts each distinct bug, fast-tracks a Mission per bug straight to the Plan stage (skipping Align, Research, and Validate), and links them all to the referenced parent Mission with the lcars:linked label. The human is expected to name the parent Mission; if none is referenced it asks which active Mission to link against first. Use when the captain runs `lcars log`, says they found a bug / bugs against a mission, or wants to file bug(s) discovered while a Mission is in flight.
- lcars-pause: Pause or resume a running LCARS Mission at a safe boundary — user-initiated pause/resume (ADR-005, PRD §5.10). `lcars pause <id>` halts a Mission cleanly: it sets a `paused` flag in state.json and applies the `lcars:paused` label, so the driver stops advancing at the next safe boundary — between Stages, or between waves/tickets in Implement — and NEVER hard-kills a worker mid-step. The Mission stays put until resumed; `lcars status` shows it with the ⏸ paused glyph and the bare `lcars` driver will not auto-pick it. `lcars resume <id>` clears the flag, removes the `lcars:paused` label, and re-enters the driver from the recorded stage. Both verbs are idempotent (double-pause / double-resume safe; resuming a non-paused Mission is a clean no-op that still drives). Use when the captain runs `lcars pause <id>` / `lcars resume <id>`, asks to pause / hold / halt / stop a Mission for now, or to resume / un-pause / continue a paused Mission.
- lcars-resolve-logs: Resolve every bug logged against a parent Mission in one batch — the Mission Log resolver. Takes a parent Mission that has N linked bug Missions (filed via `lcars log` during the parent's Verify), decides a sensible resolution order, drives each bug one-by-one to its Verify gate by delegating to the existing `lcars run` driver, and then raises EXACTLY ONE consolidated re-verify human gate plus ONE notification on the parent — instead of N scattered Verify gates. If a bug escalates mid-batch (a cap-exhausted ticket, a scope change, etc.) the batch pauses at that bug, surfaces its question in the `lcars answer` inbox, and resumes from the remaining bugs once you have answered. Adds no new stage logic. Use when the captain runs `lcars resolve-logs <parent>`, asks to resolve / clear / work through the bugs logged against a Mission, or wants the logged bugs of a Mission driven to a single re-verify gate.
- lcars-respond: Answer an LCARS Mission's awaiting-human gate, walk-away style. When a stage escalates — Research over its 20-question cap, Validate on a scope change, Plan Review after three failed rounds, or Implement after a ticket's five attempts — it parks the Mission with `lcars:awaiting-human` and a pending question. `lcars respond` (no id) lists every Mission awaiting the captain and its question(s); `lcars respond <id>` shows that Mission's pending question(s), captures the captain's free-form answer, records it next to the question in answers.json, clears the awaiting-human gate (the stage is unchanged — the Mission stays at the stage that escalated), and removes the `lcars:awaiting-human` label so a plain `lcars run <id>` resumes that same stage and consumes the answer instead of re-asking. Use when the captain runs `lcars respond`, asks what's waiting on them / what needs an answer, or wants to answer a paused / escalated / blocked Mission.
- lcars-run: Advance an LCARS Mission through the pipeline. By default `lcars run <id>` AUTO-ADVANCES — a thin, token-free bash driver sequences the Stages back-to-back (Research → Validate → Plan → Plan Review → Schedule → Implement), each spawned as a cold isolated worker, and stops only at a human gate, firing a walk-away notification. It halts when a Stage escalates a question (awaiting-human), at the Verify review gate, at an `align` feedback re-entry (an interactive re-grill), or on an error; `lcars run <id> --step` advances exactly one Stage (the old one-at-a-time behaviour, for debugging). Research reads the PRD, generates 0–20 questions, dispatches stateless research subagents, and saves their findings; Validate synthesises those findings against the PRD into a validated plan, escalating scope changes to the human; Plan decomposes the validated plan into small, vertical-slice tickets in plan.json; Plan Review runs a fresh reviewer over those tickets alone, approving them to Schedule or looping back to Plan with objections (escalating to the human after three rounds); Schedule builds the ticket dependency graph into sequential waves, opens one GitHub sub-issue per ticket, and advances to Implement; Implement processes the waves sequentially, running each ticket through an adversarial Test Writer → Implementer pair (iterating up to 5 attempts, flagging the human on failure) and advancing to Verify when every ticket is green; and Verify prints the captain's pre-ship summary and the two next moves, then stops at the h…
- lcars-status: Show the LCARS command-and-control view — every active Mission in this repo as a table with its stage, GitHub issue, and any paused / awaiting-human status, plus the pending questions the captain still needs to answer. Use when the user runs `lcars status`, asks what missions are active / in flight, what's waiting on them, or wants the kanban / board view of LCARS missions.
- lcars-update: Bring an already-initialized LCARS repo up to the current schema without clobbering the captain's customizations. Creates any MISSING GitHub labels and adds any MISSING config.json keys with their defaults, while preserving every existing value (customized testCommand / model / comprehensionBudget) and leaving missions/ untouched. Also migrates a stale LCARS-generated copy-based vitest testCommand (the incompatible `.lcars-tests` copy-staging form) to the in-place equivalent, preserving its runner flags and any leading `cd`. Use when the user runs `lcars update`, asks to refresh / upgrade / sync an existing LCARS setup after pulling new versions, or wants new labels/config keys added without re-initializing.
- lcars-version: Show the LCARS version picture — the RUNNING version of this LCARS clone (its VERSION file), the source clone's path and git state (branch, clean/dirty), and, when the current repo is LCARS-initialized, the version stamped in its config.json with a one-line verdict — `current`, `repo needs lcars update` (stamp behind OR an initialized-but-unstamped repo that predates versioning), or `unknown` (only a malformed stamp). Read-only and safe; it never runs a network fetch. Also hosts `lcars release`, the manual drift-repair that bumps VERSION + writes a CHANGELOG entry when main moved without a bump. Use when the captain runs `lcars version`, asks "what version am I on", "is my checkout / repo up to date", wants to know whether an initialized repo needs `lcars update`, or runs `lcars release` to repair unversioned drift on main.
- lcars-viewscreen: Start the LCARS Kanban web board — the bridge **viewscreen**, a local, browser-based command-and-control view of every active Mission (PRD §5.1–5.2, §6; ADR-001/002/003/007). `lcars viewscreen` (alias `lcars serve`, the older power verb that still works) launches a Python-3-stdlib-only daemon (NO pip/npm/build step) that serves a vanilla LCARS-themed static front end rendering the Kanban board: all active Missions as cards in their correct Stage columns, each with one cost pill + two difficulty pills (reasoning + implementation, low=teal/med=amber/high=red), awaiting-you and paused card states, nested ticket rows, and Implement wave/ticket progress. `lcars viewscreen --open` is the one-command launcher — it boots on a free port and opens the board in your browser. It exposes a small read API (`GET /api/board`, `GET /api/mission/<id>`) plus a live channel (SSE) that pushes on state change, and — on the LOCAL adapter — operator write endpoints (file / start / pause / resume / respond / verify / log) that dispatch to the `lcars` skills; the GitHub adapter and `--read-only` keep it view-only. ONE adapter-neutral board shape backs two interchangeable read adapters (ADR-003): a LOCAL adapter parsing `.git/lcars/missions/*` (default) and a GITHUB adapter reading issues + `lcars:*` labels via `$LCARS_GH_BIN`; the front end depends only on the shape, so a hosted view-only build is a configuration away. Use when the captain runs `lcars viewscreen` or `lcars serve`, asks to open / start / launch the LCARS viewscreen / bo…
- plan-sessions: Turn one or more rough ideas into a point-and-run, multi-session build plan — a markdown doc whose every session is a self-contained, copy-pasteable orchestrator prompt you can hand to a fresh AI session ("Read XX.md and implement session NN as the orchestrator; don't write any code yourself"). It first reads the target codebase, then grills you to alignment, then slices the work into small, independently-testable sessions (splitting any that are too big), each driven by an orchestrator that spawns implementor + tester sub-agents and never writes code itself. Use when the user runs `/plan-sessions`, says "plan this as sessions", "sessionize this idea", "break this into build sessions", or hands over a feature/refactor/initiative they want decomposed into hand-off-able chunks rather than built right now.
- run-session: Execute one session from an lcars-dev session-plan doc as its orchestrator, with a confirm-first briefing. Resolves "the next session" from roadmap.md's status table (or takes an explicit "session NN"), reads out the session number, a plain-English description of what it will build, and its TEST MODE (stubbed tests only / scoped single-engine drive / dual-CLI drive / buddy run needing the captain at the browser), waits for the captain's confirmation, then runs pre-flight checks and assumes the orchestrator role exactly as the doc's execution model prescribes. Use when the captain says "run next session", "run session NN", "what's the next session", or points at a *-dev.md file and asks to execute a session from it.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
